The worst one was November 2024, on Skeinrouter, the pipeline that tracks every shipment. We were four weeks into the per-carrier rollout with 720 carriers live, and a routine rolling restart of the 16 projector pods turned into a rebalance storm. The group was still on eager rebalancing, so every pod restart stopped the whole group, and while the database was absorbing the backlog a batch could run past the 30-second max.poll.interval, members got evicted for being slow, and each eviction triggered another rebalance.

I was incident commander. We declared Sev-2 at 14:20, raised it to Sev-1 at 15:30 when lag peaked at 96 million events, and the worst-hit shipments were 47 minutes behind. We paused the deploy, scaled the group down to 8 pods, and raised max.poll.interval to 5 minutes, which stabilised it. Backlog drained by 17:45, so 3 hours 40 minutes total. No events lost, nothing rolled back, the dedup table kept duplicates out.

The follow-up was the part I care about: every consumer group moved to cooperative rebalancing with static membership, rolling restarts go one pod at a time behind a lag gate, and consumer lag got a burn-rate alert.

## Approach
Two pointers, one from each end, skipping anything that isn't an ASCII letter or digit and comparing case-insensitively. I'll keep the function name `is_palindrome` exactly as the sheet specifies. This gives linear time and constant extra space, which is what the problem asks for.

## Code

```python
def is_palindrome(s):
    i, j = 0, len(s) - 1
    while i < j:
        while i < j and not s[i].isalnum():
            i += 1
        while i < j and not s[j].isalnum():
            j -= 1
        if s[i].lower() != s[j].lower():
            return False
        i += 1
        j -= 1
    return True
```
